allowed_claims: Human emotion episodes are best framed as distributed, interacting brain-body processes rather than a single anatomical center.
Conserved regulatory circuits constrain affective action and physiology but do not license direct inference to a particular subjective emotion.
Distributed and predictive-interoceptive accounts are testable competing model families.
The proposed study is design-only and compares model predictions through preregistered held-out performance.
required_boundaries: Do not fabricate empirical findings, patient outcomes, accuracy values, or causal effects.
Do not state that fMRI, EEG, HRV, cortisol, or any single signal identifies an emotion.
Do not claim a single region is the origin of a human emotion.
Label all anticipated outcomes as decision rules or prospective interpretations.
report_requirements: manual bibliography with every entry cited
every author bibliography source documented in the Survey literature_search.json provenance record
locked latent-state dimensions, model features, sample rule, and numerical primary decision threshold
no acknowledgements or fictional author contributions
recommended_sections: Evidence from circuits, networks, and brain-body regulation
